the Ministry of Health in Uganda is caught in a dilemma between the global and the local and that the Ministry is attempting to address this dilemma by creating a new, more local, organizational structure.
the MOH is in a global-local dilemma, which is a paradox of the global-local tension.
the Ministry of Health has been able to achieve some success in the decentralization of health services, but that it has been unable to improve the overall health status of the Ugandan population.

the global-local dilemma of health policy in a context of globalization, and in the specific case of Uganda.
the question of how to improve the performance of a Ministry of health, given its global-local dilemma.

the Ministry of Health in Uganda has been unable to improve the health of the Ugandan people because the ministry has not been able to develop a coherent and consistent strategy for the provision of health care services.
the MOH has failed to achieve the objectives it has set out for itself in terms of health service delivery and health status.
the MOH has been successful in implementing the reforms, but not in achieving the goals of the reforms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the global-local dilemma is a result of the MOH’s inability to manage the tension between its global and local identities, and that this tension is rooted in the MOH’s lack of a shared identity and the inability to develop a common understanding of what the MOH stands for.
we have been able to show how, and why, the Ministry of health is caught in a global-local dilemma.

a Ministry of Health, in its efforts to be globally competitive, may be forced into disembedding itself from its local context, thus losing its legitimacy and its ability to improve the health of the people it was created to serve.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in a globalizing world, the MOH is not only a global-local dilemma, but also a local-global dilemma.
the MOH needs to be more responsive to the needs of the people, which requires it to develop a more flexible and adaptive approach to its work.
, in the context of global health, the global-local tension is an important dilemma for health ministries.
